I have been lucky enough to be an outpatient of Dirk at New Paradigm. What a unique opportunity!

The setting
The setting of the centre is truly special, nestled within a superb garden that Khanittha, his wife, looks after so beautifully. The atmosphere alone feels healing, calm and uplifting. 😌

Dirk as a therapist and person
Regarding Dirk himself, what a grounded, kind, generous and knowledgeable gentleman. I always left their place radiating with positivity and warmth. 🤩

When I arrived vulnerable, both Dirk and Khanittha looked after me with great care, almost like an uncle and auntie. He gave me his moxa box, and she even massaged my shoulder… This was not part of the treatment, but a gesture that clearly came from the kindness of their hearts.

The therapeutic work
I ended up having fewer EMDR sessions than initially predicted, but our work was rich and multidimensional: we also talked, I received Bach flower drops prepared personally by Dirk, and I experienced alpha light therapy. After each visit, I received a complete and thoughtful report, which I deeply appreciated.

What particularly impressed me was how Dirk was willing to go against his own financial interests (reducing the number of sessions and giving me his moxa rolls, etc.) simply to ensure that I had the freedom and confidence to keep moving forward. 💪

Professionalism and philosophy
Dirk is highly specialised and extremely experienced. I would recommend him and New Paradigm to any of my friends without hesitation.

Moreover, the philosophy of New Paradigm itself is special: comprehensive, straightforward and very effective. I feel deep gratitude to the universe, and to Dirk, for enabling me to discover this true corner of heaven for people in need of guidance, support and encouragement. 🥰

The days spent at New Paradigm  will forever live in my heart. The place was absolutely beautiful, surrounded by nature and a calming atmosphere.
The daily schedule was well-balanced, with meditation sessions starting at dawn, walks in nature, yoga, exercise, pool, sauna, ice baths and massage sessions. The meals were prepared with so much love and care, Kae’s recipes did way more than fuel our bodies! They filled our hearts with joy every time we sat down to eat.

Sonny was amazing and very knowledgeable teaching yoga, his calm energy is contagious. Dirk’s guidance, support, knowledge and dedication to pass on the tools and practices  I needed to continue creating a path to a more sustainable, productive and happy life, will forever be with me.

I honestly didn’t even know what EMDR was when I first got there. I was struggling with intense germaphobia that had started to take over my life. EMDR helped me uncover and release deep fears that I didn’t even fully realize were there.It wasn’t always easy, but it was incredibly effective. For the first time in years, I feel free — free from the constant anxiety, rituals, and avoidance. I can live my life again without fear controlling everything.

Day by day, I felt more centered and present, I felt renewed and deeply connected to myself.
I would highly recommend New Paradigm to anyone looking for a genuine, transformative life experience. It’s an experience that brought me peace and clarity in a way I’ll never forget.

New Paradigm’s program successfully blends mindfulness practices with modern trauma modalities to create space for new growth and a new sense of hope. Some of the philosophies (waking early, observing silence for the majority of the day, restricted electronics access) may seem intense at first.   After completing the program, I would not want it any other way and know it would not be as effective without them.

Dirk has a kind of mindful maverick quality to him that makes him a very effective therapist. While grounded in researched backed methods like meditation and EMDR, he diverges from the conventional strategies of talk therapy and seeks to dive into the root of the issue without wasting time with extraneous tangents. He will challenge you, sometimes directly, but never without compassion and your best interest at heart. I found this to be a refreshing approach compared to past experiences with traditional psychologists. After all, most of us have come to New Paradigm’s gate because the conventional methods haven’t yielded much success. It is clear that all the pieces of the program have been well thought out to work together and were fine tuned over many years and many patients. Try to remain open minded, listen more than speak and slowly put the ideas into practice over the two weeks.

When the work is challenging, sustenance is all the more important and that’s where Kae comes in to the program with her amazingly delicious, healthy meals and afternoon snacks. Gratitude comes easier in the morning when you know you have three of her meals to enjoy during the day. There is also a fun cooking class towards the end of the retreat and recipes to take home!

Sonny is the yoga and fitness instructor who can generally be seen working hard and uplifting people with his positive spirit. He really is the definition of diligence and his morning walks, albeit feeling painfully early at first, became something I looked forward to.

If you’re feeling stuck or can’t move on from the past, I would recommend New Paradigm as a potential catalyst for a healthier perspective. None of us can change the past, but we can remodel our view of it to better suit a positive path moving forward. Thanks for all the wisdom, care, food, memories and good laughs.

All the best to you Dirk, Kae and Sonny,

Sean

I am a workaholic - have known this about myself for many years. And, my long term career in the US entertainment industry has been a perfect outlet for my addiction.

What I've also known about myself for many years is there were some deeply traumatic events in childhood and early adulthood that weren't properly addressed resulting in a C-PTSD diagnosis at the end of last year.

And, it all came crashing down at once. After many, many years of running myself into the ground, I had a major life event at the start of 2025 that I couldn't put my head down and work through - the end of a long term relationship. The lack of foundation having never done "the work" ultimately led to a mutually agreed separation of employment at the same time.

And I'm grateful it did -- because without those two things happening concurrently, I'm not sure I ever would've taken the time to stop, center myself, and face the trauma I had been trying to outrun for many years.

In researching places to go, I heard about New Paradigm through a mutual friend who had a friend that went through the program and called it "life changing." I made an inquiry immediately as I was desperate to get on the first flight out of the US so I could "fix it" and get back to the grind.

It didn't quite work out that way. There were a lot of things I needed to "fix" within myself on home soil first. I spoke to Dirk for the first time in February and we decided together that I needed to be a bit more emotionally stabilized before making the 26 hour trip to attend the program. So, I started regular counseling sessions with him and began to dive in to EMDR.

I dedicated every minute of the next 3 months prepping for my trip which was scheduled for May. I felt like a different person and that all the "healing" I'd done would make the program a breeze.

It wasn't. It was hard. Really hard (especially the first week). And my deep seated need to try to control my environment was the first major hurdle. I had developed hyper vigilance over the years as a form of protection to keep myself safe, not realizing it was doing exactly the opposite. I quickly realized that this wasn't my show and I wasn't in control - but that wasn't an easy surrender.

The second major hurdle was the surrender of all forms of technology. When that happened, my brain kicked into ruminations lasting what felt like every hour of the day from sun up to sun down. Dirk worked with me using methods to try to break the ruminations, but they were incessant. And my brain? It was focused solely on my relationship dissolving. The grief and shame that I had for not showing up differently as a partner due to my burnout / depression from my job. Guilt for not going to therapy sooner when I was being pushed to do it. The resentment for how it ended. We did a lot of EMDR around it, but still there was little relief.

After about the 9th day Dirk had a talk with me and said "we're going to cut the fuel line to what's going on. There are all these fires around you that we're putting out, but we need to cut the gas." So, we went deeper and back to childhood where we found the root cause of the issue.

Adandonment. Feelings of unworthiness. Unresolved issues with my mom that mirrored some issues in my romantic relationship. And once we did EMDR around those things, the clouds started to lift. Now, nearly a month of from the program having had some time for the EMDR to really set in and lots of reflection, I feel good. Really good. In fact, I'd say my time time at New Paradigm was life changing.

I learned more about myself in 14 days than I had in the previous 38 years. I can clearly see when my work addiction developed, why, and how my lack of relationship to self led me to a REALLY dark place. My focus now is on implementing the tools to aid in my recovery and I know for absolute certainty that I will NEVER be in the position I was in at the start of the year -- because now I have a foundation. I know who I am and I love myself. I highly recommend New Paradigm - it was the best thing to ever happen to me.

New Paradigm has taught me so much. I now step forward with determination, ready to cross whatever bridges, paths, or mountains I may encounter on this great adventure of life.
The lessons I’ve learned—and unlearned—have helped me pave a brighter path for my future, as I learn to truly live in the present.

The most memorable lesson, one I hold closest to my heart, is finally learning how to be gentle with myself.

Thank you all for your loving guidance, and for showing me what it truly means to be alive.

With loving-kindness 🙏

Throughout my life and professional career, I never felt that I needed professional help. Somehow, I always managed challenging situations myself, both in my personal and in my work life. A few months ago, however, I started to have mental blockages, strong and constant neck pain and I felt an emotional exhaustion beyond anything I had experienced before. It took me a while to realise that I was “burned out” on several levels and that a beach holiday with the family would not be enough to put me back into shape. In retrospect, no wonder, given that I work and live most of the time, away from my wife and children, in a “frontier” country that currently is at war with itself. Over there, daily life and work means daily crisis management and dealing with a lot of negativity, with varying intensity, and over a long period of time. Luckily, I realised that I need professional help and started do the research, looking for a program that I could join and that specialises in dealing with “burn out” cases and trauma, as I was quite sure that some older, traumatic experiences would need to be addressed as well, as certain thought patterns kept coming up, again and again.
In other words: I was looking for a holistic program that could address my specific needs and restore my mental strength and emotional imbalance in a relatively short time. The one program that stood out and that resonated with me instantly was the one of New Paradigm in Chiang Mai, Thailand: a maximum of 4 participants only are accepted at a time, for a 14-day retreat that sounded intense but holistic, designed to address the mental, emotional, and spiritual aspects of oneself.  To cut an incredible, life-changing experience short: I finished the program a week ago and have to say that it was the right program at the right time with the right “content”, developed and operated by the right expert: Dirk J. Lambert has grown up in the West, specialised in trauma treatment, hence understands the Western mindset, and at the same time is a two times ordained Buddhist monk who is living in Asia for more than 35 years. His uniquely designed program combines Western “treatment” models with Asian spiritual practices, resulting in a very practical and not difficult to apply “path” of recovery.  Stepping onto the path helped me to gain back my mental strength and more importantly provided me with the tools, the self- care and the confidence that will prevent me from running into the same mental “traps” again.  I could not have asked for a better retreat and for better personal guidance. Thank you, Dirk & team – you did an outstanding job!

Sometimes all it takes is letting go of what was and taking a little better care of yourself.

During an intensive retreat in Thailand, my days started at 5:30 in the morning with a quiet walk, followed by the sauna and ice bath, and then morning meditation. After breakfast, we had counseling and trauma therapy, light therapy, Muay Thai training, and Thai massages to bring our bodies back into balance.

I can honestly say this was the most beautiful and necessary experience of my life.

Not only because of the journey itself, but because of the people I met along the way. Ross and Chris from Australia and England, Sunny who guided us through all activities, Kae who cooked the most delicious food every day and cared for us with so much love, and Dirk, who guided us through deep treatments that allowed us to reconnect with our past and transform the way we carry our pain.

We were also given the chance to say goodbye to someone we miss, or to someone we were never able to say goodbye to in the past, simply because we couldn’t let go or didnt know how to.

And in between all that healing, there was so much laughter.
Chris even drew a picture of the three of us, me as Super R the Meerkat, Ross as a hamster, and Chris as the whale. We called ourselves the Holy Trinity of trauma treatment and laughed our asses off. These moments are now memories but will stay with me forever.

It was a truly magical time.

If you ever feel the need to pause, realign, or take time for yourself, I can only say this is an experience I deeply recommend.

Speaking as someone who didn’t take enough care of herself and was constantly overworking and trying to hold everything together:
take care of yourself and don’t be afraid to let go and stand alone.
When you surrender unconditionally, the most beautiful things can happen.

Love, Remke
